(a) Why called Break-even inflation? Remember,
• TIPS nominal yield = TIPS real yield + actual inflation rate.
• Treasury nominal yield = TIPS real yield + breakeven rate (expected inflation)
If actual inflation > breakeven rate → TIPS outperform nominal Treasuries → arbitrage
If actual inflation < breakeven rate → Nominal Treasuries outperform TIPS → arbitrage
If actual inflation = breakeven rate → Both give the same real return → indifferent

(b) Why Break-even inflation ≈ Expected future inflation?
Because it reflects the market’s consensus forecast for future inflation.
• If investors expect (future) inflation > breakeven rate, they buy TIPS/sell Treasuries,
   pushing breakeven rate up to match expectations, vice versa.

pages.title: 2.1. The Shapes of Yield Curves
pages.explainHtml:
曲线形态：向上（正常）、平坦、倒挂（inverted）、驼峰等。倒挂常被当成衰退预警信号（短端高于长端）。

解释形态要结合：预期未来短端路径、期限溢价、供需与央行操作。

易错点：倒挂是统计规律不是物理定律；要同时看倒挂深度与持续时间。

2.1. The Shapes          b. Increasing Yield Curve
of Yield Curves                  Signals growth and inflation expectations.
                                 • Common in recovery or boom phases.
                  •   Expectation: Investors expect strong
                      economy growth and rising inflation,
                      anticipating the central bank to raise rates to
                      cool the economy.
                  •   Risk: Holding long-term bonds risks losing
                      value to inflation and missing higher future
                      rates if central bank hikes.
                  •   Action: Investors sell long-term bonds or
                      demand higher long-term yields to
                      compensate these risks.
                  •   Result: Long-term bonds prices fall, yields
                      rise, and the yield curve increases.

2.1. The Shapes of Yield Curves

A Short Summary
   •   Flat Curve: Economic uncertainty or stability.

   •   Upward Curve: Economic growth, long-term inflation.

   •   Downward Curve: Economic slowdown or recession.

   •   Humped Curve: Transitional phase, uncertainty about short-
       term vs. long-term economic conditions.

Properties of                  Yield Curve change –Part1
YCs
Let’s discuss if there are common factors that can explain the yield curve
change, specifically, using principal components analysis (PCA) to model YCs
(Factor model). Why consider PCA?

1. High Correlation Allows Dimension Reduction
• Interest rates across maturities move together due to common factors like
   growth, inflation, and policy. This allows us to use fewer common factors
   instead of analyzing each rate individually.

2. Redundancy Supports PCA
• Rate movements are highly similar, meaning most of the variation in the
   yield curve can be captured by a few principal components—often
   representing the level, slope, and curvature of the curve.

PCA explains movements using independent factors.

E.g. A 3-Factor PCA Approximation For Yield Curve Changes:
                      𝜟𝑹 𝒕, 𝜽𝒌 ≈ 𝒄𝟏𝒌 𝑪𝟏𝒕 + 𝒄𝟐𝒌 𝑪𝟐𝒕 + 𝒄𝟑𝒌 𝑪𝟑𝒕
𝐶𝑡1 : Level factor (parallel shifts)
𝐶𝑡2 : Slope factor (twists)
𝐶𝑡3 : Curvature factor (butterfly movements)

The components have been ordered such that 𝐶𝑡1 corresponds to the largest
fraction of the total variance, 𝐶𝑡2 to the second largest and 𝐶𝑡3 to the third
largest.

The factor model reduces complexity, capturing the most important
information in the yield curve.

pages.title: 4. Yield Curve Management
pages.explainHtml:
曲线形态：向上（正常）、平坦、倒挂（inverted）、驼峰等。倒挂常被当成衰退预警信号（短端高于长端）。

解释形态要结合：预期未来短端路径、期限溢价、供需与央行操作。

易错点：倒挂是统计规律不是物理定律；要同时看倒挂深度与持续时间。

pages.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
pages.explainHtml:
总结页请当成考前速查卡：能用自己的话复述每一条，才算真懂。

对照左边要点，问自己：对应公式是什么？适用假设是什么？常见反例是什么？
pages.excerpt:
Summary & Key Takeaways

• The yield curve shows interest rates for different bond
  maturities.
• Its shape helps predict economic trends like growth or
  recession.
• Three main factors drive yield curve movements: level, slope,
  and curvature.
• Central banks use tools like QE, YCC, and forward guidance to
  influence the curve.
• The yield curve is a key indicator, influencing and reflecting
  growth, inflation, and financial stability.
